segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but when they went in they did not find the body.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were at a loss about this, suddenly two men in dazzling clothing stood beside them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were terrified and bowed their faces to the ground, but the men said to them,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Why do you look for the living among the dead?

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: He is not here, but has been raised. Remember how he told you while he was still in Galilee,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful people and be crucified and on the third day rise.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they remembered his words,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and returning from the tomb they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them. They kept telling the apostles these things.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But these words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe the women.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping to look in, he saw the linen cloths by themselves, and he went home, wondering at what had happened.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now that same day two of them were on their way to a village called Emmaus, sixty stadia from Jerusalem,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they were talking with each other about all these things that had taken place.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were talking and discussing, Jesus himself came near and walked along with them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What are these words you are exchanging with each other as you walk?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They stood still, looking gloomy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then one of them, named Cleopas, answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who has not learned what has happened there in these days?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What things?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “The things about Jesus the Nazarene, who was a prophet powerful in deed and word before God and all the people,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death, and crucified him.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But we were hoping that he was the one who was going to set Israel free. Yes, and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: What is more, some women of our group astounded us. They were at the tomb early in the morning,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and when they did not find his body, they came back saying that they had even seen a vision of angels, who say that he is alive.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Some of those with us went off to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How foolish you are, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Was it not necessary for the Messiah to suffer these things and enter into his glory?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them the things about himself in all the Scriptures.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came near the village where they were going, and he acted as though he were going farther.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they urged him strongly, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Stay with us, because it is nearly evening and the day is already far gone.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he went in to stay with them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had reclined at the table with them, he took the bread and said the blessing, and he broke it and began giving it to them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him, and he vanished from their sight.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to each other,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Were not our hearts burning within us as he was talking to us on the road, as he was opening the Scriptures to us?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem, and they found the eleven and those with them gathered together,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “The Lord really has been raised, and has appeared to Simon!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they themselves related what had happened on the road and how he was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were saying these things, he himself stood among them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Startled and terrified, they thought they were seeing a ghost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Look at my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Touch me and see, because a ghost does not have flesh and bones as you see that I have.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: [And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they still could not believe it for joy and were amazed, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you have anything here to eat?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They gave him a piece of broiled fish,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he took it and ate it in front of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “These are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you: that everything written about me in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms must be fulfilled.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This is what is written: the Messiah is to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and turning back and forgiveness of sins are to be proclaimed in his name to all the nations—beginning from Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are witnesses of these things.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And look, I am sending the promise of my Father upon you. But you, stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands he blessed them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was blessing them, he parted from them [and was carried up into heaven].

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they [worshiped him and] returned to Jerusalem with great joy,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they were continually in the temple, blessing God.

notes.note: Luke calls the figures “men,” but their dazzling clothing marks them as heavenly messengers, and verse 23 refers to them as angels. Their words are treated here as angelic speech.

notes.phrase: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb
notes.note: This verse is missing from a small group of witnesses, mainly Codex Bezae and some Old Latin copies, and older critical editions doubted it. It is present in the earliest surviving copies and the great majority of manuscripts, and most scholars now accept it as original. Several short phrases elsewhere in this chapter have a similar pattern of evidence.
A stadion was roughly 185 meters, so sixty stadia is about seven miles or eleven kilometers. Some manuscripts read “one hundred and sixty,” and the site of Emmaus is uncertain.

The verb means to live somewhere as a foreigner or temporary resident, and Cleopas probably takes the stranger for a Passover pilgrim. The Greek can also be read “Are you the only one living in Jerusalem who does not know,” or “Are you only a visitor to Jerusalem, that you do not know.”

The traditional “redeem” is now heard mainly as a term for salvation from sin. In the Greek Old Testament the verb is used of God freeing Israel from slavery in Egypt and from its enemies, and the two disciples are voicing a hope for the nation’s deliverance. Most translations keep “redeem”; the meaning itself is not disputed.

The Greek word is the one traditionally rendered “Christ.” Here it is a title for the anointed king Israel expected, and the question is what that figure had to undergo, so “Messiah” conveys what a first-century hearer understood. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels and keep “Christ” where it functions as a name.

The Greek has no object. At a Jewish meal the blessing over bread is addressed to God, who is praised for providing it; it is not pronounced on the bread. The same verb is rendered “blessed” in verse 50 and “blessing” in verse 53.

Most manuscripts, and most translations, continue “and said to them, ‘Peace be with you.’” The Greek edition translated here omits the words, following a small group of witnesses, on the view that they were added from John 20:19. Many scholars regard them as original to Luke.

The Greek word is the ordinary word for “spirit,” which older translations keep here. In this context it means the disembodied spirit of a dead person, for which the natural English word is “ghost.” Many modern translations do the same.

notes.phrase: [And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.]
notes.note: The brackets mark words that the Greek edition translated here regards as doubtful. The verse is missing from a few witnesses, chiefly Codex Bezae and some Old Latin copies, and closely resembles John 20:20. It is found in the earliest and most numerous manuscripts, and many scholars accept it as original.

“Repentance” now suggests mainly feeling sorry. The Greek word carries the prophets’ call to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct. Most translations keep “repentance” as an established term that readers understand to include a change of life.

The same Greek word means both “nations” and “Gentiles,” the non-Jewish peoples. “All the nations” is used here because the scope is the whole world, starting from Jerusalem; “all the Gentiles” is also a possible reading.

The bracketed words here and in verse 52 are absent from a few early witnesses and are marked as doubtful in the Greek edition translated here. Most manuscripts, including the earliest, contain them, and most recent scholars accept them as original.

candidates.reason: The aorist passive of Jesus’ resurrection can be rendered “was raised” (by God) or “has risen,” and it should be consistent across the Gospels, Acts and Paul, and distinct from ἀνίστημι.
“Redeem” versus “set free” or “ransom” affects this verb and its cognates (λύτρον, λύτρωσις, ἀπολύτρωσις) in Luke, Paul, Hebrews and 1 Peter.
At meals translators split between “blessed it,” “said the blessing” and “gave thanks,” and the choice recurs in the feeding and Last Supper accounts.
“Preach” and “proclaim” alternate in English versions for a verb that occurs throughout the Gospels, Acts and the letters.
“Forgiveness,” “remission” and “release” all appear for this noun, and Luke 4:18 uses it for the release of captives, so one policy is needed.
